reason.unreachable: Network is up, internet is not

footer.autostart: Start with computer (in the background, tray)

update.installLater: Installs on restart or the next time the app closes

diag.title: Where is the problem?
diag.intro: Check every link of the connection — if the internet goes down, you'll see where it breaks. The check also runs automatically on disconnect.

adapter.dhcp: The router didn't assign an IP address

router.blocked: Doesn't answer probes, but the connection works

dns.system: The system DNS server doesn't respond

adapter-off.title: The computer isn't connected to a network
adapter-off.advice: Check that Wi-Fi is on or the cable is plugged in.

adapter-dhcp.title: The computer isn't connected to a network
adapter-dhcp.advice: Wi-Fi/cable is connected, but the router didn't assign an address. Restart the router or turn Wi-Fi off and on.

router.title: The router doesn't respond
router.advice: Restart the router (unplug it for 10 seconds). On Wi-Fi, move closer to the router.

internet.title: The problem is on the provider's side
internet.advice: The router works, but the internet doesn't reach it. Restart the router; if that doesn't help, contact your provider.

dns-server.title: DNS isn't working
dns-server.advice: The internet is up, but your DNS server doesn't respond. Change DNS to 1.1.1.1 or 8.8.8.8 in your network settings.

dns.title: DNS isn't working
dns.advice: The internet is up, but names don't resolve. Restart the router; a firewall or VPN may be blocking DNS.

captive.title: Wi-Fi requires sign-in
captive.advice: Open a browser — a sign-in page will appear (hotel, café, office).

web.title: Web pages don't open
web.advice: There is a connection, but HTTP is blocked. Check your VPN, proxy or firewall.

ok.title: Everything is fine
ok.advice: Every link of the connection works.

lan.hint: NetWatch user. A phone in sleep mode may not always appear.

verdict.excellent: Excellent — 4K video, gaming and large files without problems.
verdict.good: Good — HD video, video calls and gaming will work fine.
verdict.fair: Fair — browsing and video calls, but high quality may stutter.
verdict.poor: Weak — video and calls may freeze.

speed.error: The test failed — check your internet
speed.hint: The test runs against the nearest Cloudflare server (about 20 seconds) and uses from tens to hundreds of MB of traffic, depending on your speed.

sentence.one: {when} the internet went down {count} time, {total} in total.
sentence.other: {when} the internet went down {count} times, {total} in total.

history.monitored: Monitored: {time} — time when the computer was off or asleep isn't counted.
history.clearConfirm: Delete the whole outage history? This can't be undone.
history.appClosed: the app was closed during the outage

notify.offlineBody: Connection lost. Waiting for it to come back…
notify.bgTitle: NetWatch is running in the background
notify.bgBody: It keeps checking the internet. To open it or quit — use the icon next to the clock.

report.title: Internet connection report
report.none: The internet didn't go down during this period.

sentence.one: During this period the internet went down {count} time, {total} in total.
sentence.other: During this period the internet went down {count} times, {total} in total.

report.providerPart: Of these, {count} on the provider's side (the router worked, the internet didn't).
report.note: Uptime is counted only for the time NetWatch was running ({time}); time when the computer was off or asleep isn't counted. The internet is checked every 1–2 seconds against several public servers. Diagnostics check the router, public IPs (1.1.1.1, 8.8.8.8), DNS and HTTP.
report.approx: * The app was closed during the outage — the end time is approximate.

csv.approx: The app was closed during the outage — end time is approximate
